topic: Typography and Color Theory for Interfaces
learningObjectives: Select typography that supports readability and interface hierarchy.
Apply basic color theory to interface components.
Create accessible and visually consistent text and color combinations.

activities.title: Typography Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of an interface type system.

content.concept: Typography systems define font families, sizes, weights, line heights, and hierarchy for readable interfaces.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Type Scale Slider
activities.instruction: Adjust the type scale and observe hierarchy.

content.concept: A consistent type scale creates predictable differences between headings, labels, body text, and supporting content.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Color Role Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each color to its interface role.

content.concept: Interface colors can communicate actions, states, emphasis, information, and brand identity.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Contrast Checker Lab
activities.instruction: Adjust contrast until the text becomes readable.

content.concept: Sufficient contrast improves readability and supports users with visual accessibility needs.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
